items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. A government pilot is available. The vessel’s ETA should be given 6 hours in advance through Ternate Coast Radio Station or directly by VHF to the pilot station on VHF channel 12. Berthing is only available during daylight hours only.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchoring is prohibited in an area surrounding the oil depot and CBM berth as best seen on the chart. Entry prohibited for Vessels not using the facilities surrounding the CBM berth at Jambula.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory. There is no pilot at Pulau Gebe. Vessels should advise their ETA to their general agent and local agent at least 48 hours prior to arrival, confirming at least 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory unless proceeding to the anchorage. The pilot normally boards in the anchorage. Tugs are available.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The vessel’s main engines must be maintained ready to allow for immediate departure in the event of an emergency. Vessels more than 20 years in age are not accepted unless, during a previous transfer, the vessel loaded without incident. An ETA should be sent on departure from last port of call and 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: A 10.1m shoal was reported about 15 miles WSW of Pulau Yaan. From S, the best channel is E of Yef Pelee (Pulau Polee) (2°12'S., 130°15'E.), an island about 7.5 miles S of Tanjung Wafani, then E of Kaoenoet Sollon (2°10'S., 130°20'E.), a rock 62m high and about 2.5 miles NE of the E end of Yef Pelee, then between Batu and Mate, about 2.75 miles farther NNE.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The islet is reported to be a good radar target up to a distance of 22 miles. The 617m and 670m summits N of Tanjung Salia are good marks. On both sides of Tanjung Salia there is an almost con - tinuous line of sandy beaches with plains between them and the hills. At Tanjung Liboli, the coast becomes rocky again.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is available but not compulsory for the oil terminal. Berthing and unberthing is performed during daylight hours only.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards about 1.2 mile W of Joos Sudarso Pier. The pilot boat is stationed in Teluk Ambon and can be requested by radio or by displaying the International Code Flag G. A doctor boards with the pilot. Radio pratique can be obtained.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 88 gt. Request for pilots can be made through Ambon Coast Radio Station (call sign: PKE) or on VHF channel 12. Pilot boards in Ambon Bay, 1.2 mile west of Ambon as best seen on the chart. Request for pilotage should be forwarded to the port authorities and/or agents at least 6 hours prior to arrival and 3 hours prior to departure.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: When coming from the S steer for the conspicuous summit of Pulau Seram Laut on a 056° bearing until the S beacon on Pulau Kilwaru (3°53'S., 130°54'E.), a low island about 0.5 mile ENE of Pulau Geser, is bearing about 020° (this beacon is reported difficult to identify sometimes), then alter course northward and be guided by the beacons to the anchorage.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The vessel can be guided by the beacons to the roadstead, but care must be taken to avoid the shoals in the approach to and within the roadstead. To enter Tual Roads from NW through Selat Duroa, set course for Tanjung Nigidiun from a position about 10 miles N of that point. From this position Pulau Tayandu, Pulau Er, and Tanjung Ngidiun are good landmarks.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: About 1.5 miles W of the mouth of Sungi Dosi, in which there are some islets and which is about 9 miles ENE of Sungi Api Api, there is a drying rock which must be passed on the N side. Beyond the mouth of Sungi Feraun, on the N shore about 2 miles ENE of Sungi Dosi, the N shore should be hugged, but thereafter the S shore should be closed by crossing between drying mud banks in a least depth of 5.5m.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The island is reported to be a good radar target at a distance of up to 30 miles. Two inlets penetrate the E side of the island for a distance of about 1.75 miles. Several rocky islets are off the E side of the island. An islet about 1.25 miles SE of the easternmost point of Pulau Kawe extends in a SE direction in Selat Bougainville, with a reef at its outer end.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: It is reported that a vessel drawing 5.9m can proceed to nearly all parts of the bay. The bottom is mainly soft mud. The chief off-lying dangers are a 1.8m shoal and a 6.4m shoal about 0.75 mile E and 2 miles ESE, respectively, from the W entrance point to the bay. A reef, surrounded by shoal water, is about 2.25 miles inside the entrance on the E side of the channel.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Pulau Saonek-besar may be passed on either side, but in rounding that island to the W they must give a good berth to the reef extending out from the island. The highest point of Pulau Gam and Pulau Saonek-besar hill in range bearing 282°, leading well S of the SW extremity of the ridge of reefs E of Pulau Saonek-besar and is a good mark for vessels approaching Saonek Roads anchorage from E. There is a 3.7m shoal 3 miles E of Saonek Besar.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hrs. The pilot boards in position 00°52'S., 131°13.5'E. Pilotage for tankers board in the anchorage area 2 miles NW of Tsiof Lt in 00°53.00'S., 131°10.15'E as best seen on the chart.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and should be requested from Sorong 6 hours prior to arrival. Vessels awaiting a pilot can anchor about 1.25 miles NW of the SW end of Pulau Tsiof, over a bottom of mud and coral. Vessels arriving after 1600 will wait at anchor until daylight to make the transit to the terminal.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Except for local fishing craft, the port lim - its area is a restricted area. Any vessel authorized to use the port must have a mooring master on board. The vessel’s ETA must be sent 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival. Salawati Oil Terminal (1°21'S., 130°59'E.)

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. See paragraph 5.40, Kasim Oil Terminal, for details.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: This leads close N of a 4m shoal which extends a short distance N from the reef fringing the islet off the NW end of Balbili, however, vessels exceeding a draft of 4m must pass S of Balbili. When Mehil (1°07'S., 131°10'E.) bears 100°, alter course SSW to bring the range lights on Segarau (1°10.5'S., 131°06.6'E.) and Kamoomjel, which lies 3.5 miles farther SSW, in line on a bearing of 196°; this course should lead W of the buoy moored 0.5 mile ENE of the light column on Segarau.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage for the Muturi Oil Terminal is com - pulsory for vessels over 50 tons. ETA at the outer buoy should be given at least 24 hours in advance. Pilotage at night is only by special arrangement.

notes.quote: The terminal consists of a T-headed pier 18.3m long, with a depth of 13.7m alongside; it can accommodate vessels of up to 30,000 tons, with a maximum length of 200m and a maximum draft of 10.6m.
The current always sets on to the jetty; the maximum observed rate is 4.5 knots.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The channel E of Pulau Panjang is clear of dangers, but two reefs, with depths of 1.8 to 2.7m, respectively, 6.5 and 3.75miles ESE of Tanjung Wamarusa must be avoided. These reefs show up by discoloration with good light. Vessels approaching from W can pass to within 0.5 mile of Tanjung Wamarusa on an easterly course.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory. Pilots come from Port Moresby with at least 48 hours notice. The pilot boards at position 9°50.4'S, 143°12.6'E or in case of bad weather at position 9°06.8'S, 143°19.44'E. Port of

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory; there is no pilot boarding area in the immediate vicinity of the terminal. Pilots may be provided by arrangement with Queensland Coast or Torres Strait Pilot Associations.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The vessel’s ETA should be sent 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours in advance. The pilot boards in the anchorage area 4 miles E of the Kumul Terminal Platform.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: The terminal is surrounded by a restricted area.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 30m L OA a nd available 24 hours. The pilot boards from an orange motor launch with a blue hull 0.8 mile WSW of the entrance to Basilisk Passage. In bad weather pilots board inside the passage about 0.5 mile NW from the entrance in position 9°31'55.8''N, 147°08'21.6''E.

notes.quote: With prior permission, a vessel may proceed directly to the anchorage 0.75 mile W of Manubada Island and await pilot boarding.
Pilots board in position 9°17'20.4''S, 146°51'19.8''E for the LNG terminal.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Radio frequencies used are VHF channels 6, 8, 12, and 16. Vessels should maintain listening watch on VHF channel 16 one hour prior to arrival. Vessels are normally berthed in daylight hours. Tankers at the oil and LPG berths are unberthed only during daylight hours.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Port Moresby—Inside the Barrier Reef

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory but is available with 48 hours notice from Port Moresby.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for Alotau. A request via Port Moresby Radio (P2M) should be made, giving 48 hours notice of ETA. The vessel’s arrival should be sent not less than 12 hours via Port Moresby Radio and is to be con- firmed not more than 5 hours or less than 4 hours prior to arrival, again via Port Moresby Radio.

notes.quote: The pilot boards about 0.6 mile from Sanderson Point Lighthouse.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: A depth of 7.3m was reported on the Muniara Island side of this passage. Another passage from W, reportedly used by a small vessel, is to enter between Panasesa Island and Gabuga butau Island. A depth of 5.5m was reported between these islands. Vessels then pass close to the fringing reef on the N side of Itamarina Island.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The E peak of the continuous high land of Woodlark Island, bearing 314°, is reported to lead up to the W entrance. When the W entrance has been identified, a ves - sel should steer to pass between the spit extending from the SW end of the reef on which Vaviai lies, and an unexamined shoal, in a depth 5.5m, about 0.6 mile SSW of it, passing about 0.1 mile from the reef and rounding the NW angle at the same distance, avoiding Iris Patch.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The passage is about 0.2 mile wide, and was reported to have a depth of 51m. Vessels proceeding from Moresby Strait to the Amphlett Group require local knowledge and should use the swept channel which passes NW of the group. After passing through Warrego Passage bring Talafamata Jetty bearing 242° astern, and keep it on that bearing until Cape Labilardiere bears 180°, distant about 1.25 miles, when a course of 100° should be steered, passing S of the 3.7m and 2.7m patches N of the cape.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for anchoring, berthing, and unberthing. The pilot boards on the 300° range line in position 5° 13.3’S 145° 50.2’E. The ETA at the pilot station should be sent not less than 12 hours before arrival via Port Madang, Port Moresby Radio or Rabaul Radio, and should be confirmed not more than 5 hours and not less than 4 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: The approach E of Chirimosh Island is reported to be the best. A vessel approached the harbor with Chirimosh Island bearing 179° until the Nend of Pataki Island bore 089°, when a course of 230° was steered, passing between Schimo Reef and the N end of Hedwigs Reef. Then a course of 162° was steered, keeping in mid-channel between West Point and Chirimosh Island.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory. Pilot available with 48 hours notice from Madang.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory. Pilots are available with 48 hours notice from Madang. The pilots can be contacted by telephone (675- 982-1538). The pilot boards at position 2°39.0'S, 141°18.0'E; during bad weather the pilot boards at a position with Vanimo Point bearing 240° distant 1.6 miles.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and available 24 hours for vessels over 70 gt. Vessels should send their ETA to the Port Authority 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival. Requests for pilots should be sent 6 hours prior to arrival. The Port Authority can be contacted on VHF channels 12 and 16, while the oil terminals can be contacted on VHF channels 16, 9, and 19.

notes.quote: On arrival at the entrance to Teluk Yos Sudarso, vessels are usually advised by VHF to anchor SSW of Tanjung Suaja or proceed to the pilot boarding point.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory, but is not undertaken at night. The pilot boards in the anchorage in position 1°12.2'S, 136°°05.0'E.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A prohibited anchorage area is situated near the submarine cables between Teluk Serui and Pulau Saweru. The coast is flat and sandy from a position about 4 miles NW of Teluk Serui to Pulau Janusi, the E entrance point of Teluk Kanawa. Tanjung Worui (Tanjung Woroei), about 7.5 miles WNW of Teluk Serui, and Tanjung Panduami (Tanjung Pandoeami), nearly 3 miles farther W, are covered with high trees.
